chapter_title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinders, Prisms, and Composite Solids

worksheets.title: Surface Area of Right Prisms and Cylinders

fluency_questions.prompt: Find the total surface area of each cube or rectangular prism:

A triangular prism has two triangular ends and three rectangular sides. For a prism with triangle area $6\text{ cm}^2$ at each end and three rectangles of areas $30\text{ cm}^2, 40\text{ cm}^2, 50\text{ cm}^2$, find:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The combined area of the two triangular ends ($2 \times 6$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: The combined area of the three rectangular sides ($30 + 40 + 50$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: The total surface area of the triangular prism ($12 + 120$)

parts.label: d
parts.question: The surface area if the bottom rectangle ($40\text{ cm}^2$) is on the ground and not painted

fluency_questions.prompt: Use $\text{CSA} = 2\pi rh$ to find the exact curved surface area of each cylinder in terms of $\pi$:
For a closed cylinder with radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$ and height $h = 5\text{ cm}$, find in terms of $\pi$:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The area of one circular end ($\pi r^2 = \pi \times 3^2$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: The area of both circular ends ($2\pi r^2$)

application_questions.question: A wooden storage cube in a classroom has side length $4\text{ m}$ (or $40\text{ cm}$). If each of its $6$ square faces has area $40 \times 40 = 1600\text{ cm}^2$, find the total surface area of all $6$ faces.

A soup tin is a cylinder with radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and height $h = 10\text{ cm}$. The paper label wraps around the curved side only. Calculate $2 \times \pi \times 4 \times 10$ to find the exact area of the paper label in terms of $\pi$.

A cereal box is a rectangular prism $20\text{ cm}$ wide, $30\text{ cm}$ high, and $8\text{ cm}$ deep. Calculate $\text{TSA} = 2(20 \times 30 + 20 \times 8 + 30 \times 8)$ to find the total cardboard area.

An open cylindrical drinking glass (no lid) has a flat circular base of area $9\pi\text{ cm}^2$ and a curved side of area $24\pi\text{ cm}^2$. Add these together to find the outside surface area of the glass.

reasoning_questions.question: When you unroll the curved wall of a cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h$ flat onto a table, what 2D shape does it form, and what are its length and width?
reasoning_questions.answer: It forms a rectangle whose height is $h$ and whose width is the circumference of the circle, $2\pi r$.

reasoning_questions.question: Why does an open-top cylindrical bucket have total surface area $\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$ instead of $2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$?
reasoning_questions.answer: Because it has no top lid, so there is only $1$ circular base ($\pi r^2$) instead of $2$ circular ends ($2\pi r^2$).

worksheets.title: Volume of Cylinders, Composite Solids, and Error in Measurement

fluency_questions.prompt: Use $V = A \times h$ (Cross-sectional Area $\times$ height/length) to find the volume of each prism:

parts.label: d
parts.question: Triangular prism with triangle area $12\text{ cm}^2$ and length $8\text{ cm}$

fluency_questions.prompt: Use $V = \pi r^2 h$ to find the exact volume of each cylinder in terms of $\pi$:
Each measurement is rounded to the nearest whole unit (maximum error $\pm 0.5$). Find:

parts.label: c
parts.question: The lower and upper bounds of $24\text{ m}$ (nearest $1\text{ m}$)

parts.label: d
parts.question: The absolute error if a desk is $120\text{ cm}$ long but measured as $123\text{ cm}$ ($123 - 120$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Calculate the percentage error using $\dfrac{\text{Absolute Error}}{\text{Actual Value}} \times 100\%$:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Absolute error $= 1\text{ cm}$, actual length $= 10\text{ cm}$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Absolute error $= 2\text{ m}$, actual length $= 50\text{ m}$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Absolute error $= 5\text{ g}$, actual mass $= 100\text{ g}$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Absolute error $= 3\text{ L}$, actual volume $= 60\text{ L}$

application_questions.question: A cylindrical mug has a circular base of radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and a height of $h = 10\text{ cm}$. Calculate $V = \pi \times 4^2 \times 10$ to find the exact volume in terms of $\pi$.

A concrete garden step is made of two rectangular blocks stacked together: the bottom block has volume $4000\text{ cm}^3$ and the top block has volume $2500\text{ cm}^3$. Find the total volume of concrete needed.
A student estimates the length of a cricket pitch in Brisbane as $21\text{ m}$, whereas its actual length is $20\text{ m}$. Find the absolute error and the percentage error.
A wooden block has volume $500\text{ cm}^3$. A cylindrical hole of volume $80\text{ cm}^3$ is drilled out of the middle. Subtract to find the remaining volume of wood.

reasoning_questions.question: If a cylinder is given with diameter $d = 10\text{ cm}$ and height $h = 6\text{ cm}$, why is it wrong to calculate $V = \pi \times 10^2 \times 6$? What should you do first?
reasoning_questions.answer: The formula $V = \pi r^2 h$ uses the radius $r$, not the diameter $d$. You must first halve the diameter to get $r = 5\text{ cm}$, giving $V = \pi \times 5^2 \times 6 = 150\pi\text{ cm}^3$.

reasoning_questions.question: A bag of apples is weighed as $3\text{ kg}$ to the nearest kilogram. Explain why a bag weighing $2.6\text{ kg}$ rounds to $3\text{ kg}$, and state the smallest possible weight that rounds up to $3\text{ kg}$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Any weight from $2.5\text{ kg}$ up to $3.5\text{ kg}$ is closer to $3\text{ kg}$ than to $2\text{ kg}$ or $4\text{ kg}$; the smallest weight (lower bound) is $2.5\text{ kg}$.
